label: <DEL> step of short (L=3-4) sequences built from p/k/f/u/s/n-type letters, starting with u/k/f/d/b/p
explanation: Fires only on the delimiter step (100% of mass), almost only when L=3 or 4 (96% of mass; a few at L=5, none at L>=6). Within those it acts like an additive token-content detector: it needs the first token (which is output at that step) to be one of u/k/f/d/b/p and most original tokens to come from a consonant set (p,k,f,u,s,n,r,b,d,h). Digits suppress it (81% of mass in digit-free sequences). Top activations (k p n, f k s, k u p p) are made up entirely of these letters. It never fires in the original or copy phases. Precision is low (~0.27 on dev) because many matching sequences stay below threshold, so the exact token weighting is not captured.
